title: A goal created straight after the Activate chain is accepted, not refused against a two-second-stale frame
description:
Filed by worker-2739fee7 on 2026-09-05 from task-d342a2b158764fefa8dbf2a5365e7bf7, which fixed the browser Activate chain and then hit this ONE STEP FURTHER ON. That row is BLOCKED on this one: it cannot satisfy its DoD-2 second clause ("the `goal.create_with_source` that the same draft was refused before activation is ACCEPTED after it") while this defect stands.

THE DEFECT, measured against a real daemon at `seed: "NONE"`, not inferred. After task-d342a2b1's fix the browser chain runs all FIVE steps green — `cr.activate.step.policy.install` and `cr.activate.step.project.activate` both carry data-ok="true" — and then the very next create is refused CLIENT-SIDE:

  Expected: "Goal created: Browser-only fresh start"
  Received: "goal.create_with_source is blocked until Activate the project commits. Next step: use
             the Activate project card on this screen; it drives the whole chain from the browser."
  tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts:220

THE DAEMON IS NOT THE REFUSER. `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["goal.create_with_source"] = ["project.activate"]` and `project.activate` is COMMITTED — proven by its own data-ok="true" in the same run. The refusal never reaches the wire.

THE CAUSAL CHAIN, traced file by file:
1. `createGoalDispatcher` (apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts:201-215) takes `getFrame: () => SurfaceFrame | null` and reads it ONCE, deliberately — its own comment: "ONE read of the frame: the refusal must describe the same surface the offer was looked for on, not a later poll's." With `offer === null` it returns `goalCreateRefusal(frame, kind)` WITHOUT dispatching.
2. That frame is `frameRef.current` (apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goals.tsx:85-92), refreshed by a 2000 ms poll (`POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, live-goals.tsx:33).
3. `LiveActivate` (apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activation-screen.tsx:206-211) DOES call `refresh()` when the chain settles — but that refreshes its OWN `/activation/read`, not the goals screen's independently-polled surface frame. NOTHING invalidates `frameRef`.

So for up to 2 s after a successful activation the create path refuses against a pre-activation frame. The report is a one-shot submit result, so it never self-corrects: the spec's 5 s `toHaveText` retry observed the same string 14 times. An operator who clicks New Goal promptly after Activate is told to go use the card they just used.

THE SEAM, stated but NOT ruled — pick deliberately:
(a) re-read the surface once on the refusal path in `createGoalDispatcher` before refusing (preserves the "one read per decision" intent: re-read, then look for the offer AND build the refusal on that same newer frame — this is the same idiom `driveActivationChain` already uses, "a cached offer is a stale version");
(b) give the Activate card a way to invalidate the shared frame when its chain settles (the shell already holds `boardFrame` + `reportFrame` in cordum-app.tsx:130-145, and `LivePolicy` at live-ops.tsx:115 already calls `refresh()` on the same pattern);
(c) both.

COORDINATION, and it is why task-d342a2b1 did not just fix it: `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts` and `live-goal-create.test.ts` are BOTH DIRTY with another session's in-flight work in this shared checkout. Check `git status` and coordinate with that owner before editing them.

DO NOT weaken tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts to close this. Adding a wait would mask a defect a real operator hits by clicking fast; that spec is the row that found both defects.

A test asserts the REASON, not just the outcome: with the fix removed, the create straight after activation still refuses with the daemon's own words and the refusal is the STALE-FRAME one — prove the arm goes red and quote it (global rail 1). A unit-level arm in the create path is required; the e2e alone is not enough, because a 2 s race can pass by luck.

The chosen seam is STATED with its reason in the completion record: whether the create path re-reads before refusing, whether the Activate card invalidates the shared frame, or both — and why the rejected option was rejected.

Whatever change lands preserves the existing intent that a refusal describes the SAME surface the offer was looked for on (live-goal-create.ts:203-205). If that comment stops being true, it is rewritten in the same diff rather than left contradicting the code.

THE SEAM, RULED. No files changed this step — this is the recorded ruling DoD-3 asks for.

RULING: OPTION (a) ONLY — the create path re-reads the affordance surface once before it refuses. Not (b), not (c).

WHY (a). The defect is a decision made against stale input, and it is made in exactly one place: `createGoalDispatcher` in apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts. Fixing it at that point of decision is correct for EVERY route into a create, not only the Activate-card-then-New-Goal route the e2e spec happens to walk. The frame is a 2000 ms poll of a daemon that several principals write: the Activate card is one, but a worker seat, the wrapper, a terminal `moe` invocation or a second operator in another tab can commit `project.activate` inside the same 2 s window, and in every one of those cases the operator's next click is refused against a surface the daemon has already moved past. (a) closes all of them with one change in one file.

WHY NOT (b) ALONE — invalidating the shared frame from the Activate card. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) It closes exactly ONE route: the four other principals above still race the poll, so the defect would still be reachable and the row would be closing a symptom. (2) It couples two screens through the goals screen's internals — `LiveActivate` in ops/activation-screen.tsx would have to reach the goals screen's `frameRef`, or the shell would have to grow a shared invalidation channel, to fix a bug that lives in neither of them. (3) It cannot be tested deterministically at unit level: it is a cross-component effect over a `useRef`, so its arm would be a mount-and-wait, which is exactly the by-luck evidence DoD-2 refuses. (b) does remain a legitimate UI NICETY on its own terms — the disabled create control reads the same `frameRef` (live-goals.tsx:132-ish region) and would light up sooner rather than up to 2 s later — but that is a responsiveness concern, not this defect, and it closes nothing (a) does not. If wanted it is a follow-up row.

WHY NOT (c) BOTH. Two mechanisms landed together for one defect means neither is load-bearing: a later reader cannot tell which one is holding the invariant, and a drill that removes either leaves the arm green. That is precisely how a fix rots into decoration. One mechanism, one drill, one red.

THE TRAP, AND WHY IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The row's own wording, "re-read the surface once on the refusal path", reads as if a second `getFrame()` call would do it. The re-read must therefore be an ASYNC fetch of /affordances/read.

implementationPlan.description: THE CHANGE, AND THE COMMENT THAT MUST STAY TRUE. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts (229 lines, target under 250 - keep this small). In `createGoalDispatcher`: after `goalCreateOffer(frame, kind)` returns null, re-read once via `readSurfaceOnce(setup.headers)`, look for the offer AGAIN on that newer frame, and proceed to dispatch if it is now there; only if it is STILL absent build the refusal - and build it from the NEWER frame, not the stale one. THE HAPPY PATH PAYS NOTHING: the extra round trip happens only on a path that was about to fail anyway. HANDLE THE RE-READ FAILING: `readSurfaceOnce` fetches with a timeout and can throw or answer a non-surface body. A network failure there must NOT become a confusing new error on a path the operator experiences as "create refused" - fall back to refusing on the frame you already had, which is exactly today's behaviour, so the worst case is unchanged rather than newly broken. Say in the step note which failure shapes you handled. DoD-4, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL BOOKKEEPING: the comment at :203-205 reads "ONE read of the frame: the refusal must describe the same surface the offer was looked for on, not a later poll's." That INTENT survives this change and the wording must be amended to match rather than deleted: there are now up to two reads, and the invariant is that the offer lookup and the refusal are built from THE SAME frame - the newer one when a re-read happened. Rewrite it to say that, naming why the re-read exists (a prerequisite committed between the poll and the click) so the next reader does not "simplify" it back into the defect. A comment left contradicting the code is a defect in its own right.

THE UNIT ARM, WHICH DoD-2 REQUIRES BECAUSE THE E2E CAN PASS BY LUCK. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.test.ts (DIRTY with peer WIP - append arms, do not restructure the file, and re-read their diff before writing). A 2 s race is exactly the kind of thing a green e2e run proves nothing about, so these arms must drive the sequence deterministically with an injected surface reader rather than by timing. THREE ARMS: (1) THE DEFECT'S FIX - the first frame carries NO create offer, the re-read answers a frame that DOES, and the dispatcher DISPATCHES rather than refusing. Assert the command actually went to the transport, not merely that the result was ok. (2) THE REFUSAL IS BUILT ON THE NEWER FRAME - first frame stale, re-read answers a frame that still lacks the offer but differs observably, and the refusal text reflects the SECOND frame. This is the arm that pins DoD-4's invariant: without it, a fix that re-reads for the lookup but refuses from the stale frame passes arm (1) and still lies to the operator. (3) THE RE-READ FAILS - the reader throws or times out, and the dispatcher refuses on the original frame with today's wording, no new error class leaking to the surface. FOR DoD-2's RED PROOF: with the fix removed, arm (1) must fail with the stale-frame refusal string - quote it. Assert the REASON, never just `ok === false`: the refusal text is the operator-facing artifact and it is what the e2e compares. Note that the injected reader is how these arms stay deterministic; if `readSurfaceOnce` is imported directly rather than injected, the arms cannot control it - so pass it as an optional parameter defaulting to the real helper, the same lazy-injection convention this codebase uses for `readSessions`/`readClaims` in sessions-read.ts:86-87.
implementationPlan.note:
THE UNIT ARMS. One file: apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.test.ts. APPENDED, not restructured — the peer's two rewritten refusal-copy literals at :102-116 are untouched and still pass; my work is a new `describe` block after the existing two plus one type-only import line.

FIVE ARMS, not the three the plan named. The plan's three are all present; the two extra pin invariants step 5(c)'s adversarial list asks about, and one of them catches a bug a bare try/catch would have shipped.

(1) "dispatches when the prerequisite committed after the poll that fed the frame" — THE DEFECT'S FIX. Polled frame is `blockedOn("project.activate")` (no offer, the pre-activation surface); the injected reader answers `frame()` (offer present). Asserts the command REACHED THE TRANSPORT, not merely `ok`: `sent` has length 1, `sent[0].commandId === "c1"`, `sent[0].commandKind === "goal.create"`, then `result.ok` and the exact report `"Goal created: Second goal"` — the same sentence the e2e spec compares at activation-fresh-project.spec.ts:220 — and `reader.calls === 1`.

(2) "builds the refusal from the re-read frame, not the stale one" — DoD-4's INVARIANT. Polled frame is blocked on `project.activate`; the re-read still has no offer but is blocked on `provider.probe` instead, so the two frames yield DIFFERENT sentences. Asserts `result.report` is exactly BLOCKED_ON_PROBE and explicitly `not.toBe(BLOCKED_ON_ACTIVATE)`. This is the arm that fails a half-fix which re-reads for the LOOKUP but refuses from the cached frame — that variant passes arm (1) and still describes a surface that no longer exists.

(3) "keeps the frame in hand when the re-read rejects, with no new error class" — the reader rejects with `new DOMException("signal timed out", "TimeoutError")`, the real shape `AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` produces. Asserts the report is exactly BLOCKED_ON_ACTIVATE (today's behaviour, the daemon's own prerequisite words), `not.toContain("TimeoutError")`, and nothing sent.

(4) EXTRA — "keeps the frame in hand when the re-read answers an unreadable surface". Two cases in one loop: a LAGGING/UNREADABLE frame and a DISCONNECTED one. This is the arm that would have caught a `try/catch`-only implementation: `frameOfSurface` does NOT throw on a body it cannot read (live-board-feed.ts:242-244 returns `frame("LAGGING", "UNREADABLE", ...)`), so a catch alone adopts that frame, and because `goalCreateRefusal` tests `frame.connection !== "CONNECTED"` FIRST the operator would have been told "the board is not connected to the daemon" instead of what is actually missing — strictly worse than the defect. Asserts the report stays BLOCKED_ON_ACTIVATE and is `not.toBe(NOT_CONNECTED_SENTENCE)`.

(5) EXTRA — "makes no extra request when the polled frame already carries the offer". `reader.calls === 0` on the happy path, proving the re-read lives inside the branch that was already going to fail. This answers step 5(c)'s "does the happy path make any extra request" with an assertion rather than a reading of the diff.

DETERMINISM, NOT TIMING. Every arm drives the sequence through the injected `SurfaceReader` — no fake timers, no waits, no 2 s window. That is the whole reason DoD-2 demands a unit arm: the e2e can pass by luck on a race. `readerOf(frames)` is a tiny counting stub returning frames in order (last one repeated), so an arm can assert HOW MANY reads happened as well as what they answered.

ASSERT THE REASON, NOT THE OUTCOME (global rail 1). No arm asserts only `ok === false`. Arms 2, 3 and 4 each pin an EXACT operator-facing sentence, and arms 2 and 4 additionally assert the sentence is NOT the one the wrong implementation would produce — so a second refusal layer answering first cannot keep them green. The literals BLOCKED_ON_ACTIVATE / BLOCKED_ON_PROBE are written out in the test file rather than imported from the module under test, following this file's own stated rule ("an imported literal is a fixed point a hardcoded-return mutant would satisfy", :163-174). They match the PEER's current wording ("use the Activate project card on this screen; it drives the whole chain from the browser"), not HEAD's — step 1's coordination note.

INCIDENTAL FINDING, worth knowing and not a defect: the pre-existing arm "sends nothing and reports the blocked sentence when the surface carries no offer" (:139-151) calls `createGoalDispatcher(setup, () => blocked)` with NO reader, so it now exercises the DEFAULT `readSurfaceOnce`. Under vitest that resolves a relative URL "/affordances/read" with no document base and Node's fetch rejects immediately with a TypeError — no network is attempted — which `rereadSurface` catches, so the arm still refuses on the frame in hand and still passes unchanged. It is therefore an accidental positive control that the catch arm works against the REAL helper, not only the stub. I left it exactly as it was.

Restore proof for a drill is that the file matches ITS PRE-DRILL STATE, peer hunks included: capture a SHA256 of each file BEFORE the drill (they are tracked but not clean, so `git diff` cannot distinguish your mutation from the peer's edits) and prove equality after, in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Say so explicitly rather than quoting an empty-diff proof that would be false here. TWO DRILLS: (i) remove the re-read - arm (1) must go RED with the stale-frame refusal string, quoted. That is DoD-2's proof and the row's central artifact. (ii) Re-read for the lookup but build the refusal from the STALE frame - arm (2) must go RED. If it stays green, arm (2) is not actually pinning the invariant DoD-4 asks for and must be fixed before you continue. (b) GATES - standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (the only leg that sees these files - root `pnpm test` has no `apps/**` in vitest.config.ts:32), `pnpm typecheck`, and the e2e spec run directly per step 1(d) with the foreign scheduler red disclosed. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's two owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY - and be careful here, because the peer's in-flight edits to the same files can produce red that is theirs, not yours: separate the two by whether the failing arm names your change. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: does the happy path make any extra request (it must not); what happens if the re-read answers a frame whose connection is refused; two rapid create clicks each triggering a re-read; the re-read succeeding but returning a frame OLDER than the cached one (a poll and a re-read can race - does the code prefer the newer, and how does it tell); did you touch tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts in any way (rail 2 forbids it - `git diff --stat` it and confirm zero); did you overwrite any peer hunk. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: the seam chosen and why - option (a), re-read on the refusal path, because the fix belongs at the point of decision and covers every route rather than the one the spec walks - and why (b) was rejected as a second mechanism closing nothing (a) does not; that `getFrame()` is synchronous over a poll-written ref and therefore could not have been the re-read; the amended wording of the :203-205 comment and why the invariant survives; both drill reds verbatim; the peer-dirt coordination you did; and the foreign scheduler red, disclosed with its file and line and explicitly NOT adopted.

comments.content:
SEAM RULED: OPTION (a) — AND THE ROW'S OWN WORDING HIDES A NO-OP FIX. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 2 files.

Excellent filing — the causal chain was traced file by file and every line reference held. One thing needed an architect rather than a worker, and it is not the choice between (a), (b) and (c).

## "Re-read the surface" cannot mean calling `getFrame()` again

`getFrame` is constructed at live-goals.tsx:132 as `() => frameRef.current`. That ref is **synchronous** and written **only** by the 2000 ms poll's `onFrame` (:89-92). So a second call returns **the same stale frame** — a fix that reads exactly like the row's option (a), changes nothing, and would pass a careless review while the defect ships.

The re-read must be an **async fetch**, and the sanctioned one already exists: `readSurfaceOnce(headers)` at `policy-install-port.ts:35` — *"One read of the affordance surface, for the offer at the aggregate's current version"* — re-exported by `activation-port.ts:22` under an explicit rail: *"a second fetch idiom for the same route is exactly what this row's rail forbids."*

And the headers are already in hand: `createGoalDispatcher` takes `setup: LiveSetup`, whose `headers` field is documented at `live-config.ts:38` as *"Header values for the one route the transport does not carry (/affordances/read)"* — this exact route. No new plumbing, no new parameter.

## Why (a) and not (b)

The defect is decided **at the point of decision**, so fixing it there is correct for **every** route into a create. Activate→New Goal is the route the spec walks, but a seat, the wrapper, or a second operator can commit a prerequisite between the poll and the click just as easily — and (b) leaves all of those still racing.

(b) stays a legitimate UI nicety: the disabled create control reads the same frame and would update sooner. But that is a different concern, and it closes nothing (a) does not. **Not (c)**: two mechanisms for one defect means neither is load-bearing and a later reader cannot tell which holds the invariant. If the nicety is wanted, it is a follow-up row.

## The half-fix that would still lie to the operator

Re-reading for the offer **lookup** but building the refusal from the **stale** frame passes the obvious arm while describing a surface that no longer exists. That is what DoD-4's invariant guards, and the plan pins it with its own test arm plus a drill: re-read for the lookup, refuse from the stale frame, and require that arm to go red.

The comment at :203-205 survives the change and must be **amended, not deleted** — there are now up to two reads, and the invariant becomes "the offer lookup and the refusal are built from the *same* frame, the newer one when a re-read happened."

## Two operational hazards, both re-measured at plan time

**The peer dirt is still live.** `git status` shows ` M live-goal-create.ts` and ` M live-goal-create.test.ts` — both files this row must edit — plus work-labels, work-board and activation-port. This breaks the usual drill rule: **an empty `git diff` cannot be a restore proof here**, because it is non-empty before, during and after, and cannot distinguish your mutation from the peer's edits. The plan requires a SHA256 captured before each drill and proved after, in a separate call.

**The foreign scheduler red must not be adopted.** `pnpm test:e2e:browser`'s tsc leg fails on `budget-reservation.ts(132,42)` — a committed red in a package this row does not own. Run playwright directly and disclose it; landing someone else's fix would make this row's red attribution unreadable.

One edge worth deciding rather than assuming: a poll and a re-read can race, so the re-read could answer an **older** frame than the cached one. Prefer the newer and say how you can tell — a version or timestamp comparison is honest; guessing is not.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE ROW STATED THREE SEAMS AND DELIBERATELY LEFT THE RULING TO THE ARCHITECT. Ruled: OPTION (a), re-read on the refusal path.

WHY (a): the defect is decided in `createGoalDispatcher`, so fixing it there is correct for EVERY route into a create. The Activate-then-New-Goal path is the one the spec walks, but a seat, the wrapper or a second operator can commit a prerequisite between the 2 s poll and the click just as easily, and (b) leaves all of those racing. It is also the smaller diff, in one file, using a helper that already exists.
WHY NOT (b) ALONE: invalidating the shared frame from the Activate card couples two screens through the goals screen's internals and closes exactly ONE route. It stays a legitimate UI nicety - the disabled create control reads the same frame and would update sooner - but that is a different concern from this defect and closes nothing (a) does not.
WHY NOT (c) BOTH: two mechanisms for one defect, landed together, means neither is load-bearing and a later reader cannot tell which is holding the invariant. If the nicety is wanted, it is a follow-up row.

THE TRAP IN THE ROW'S OWN WORDING, and the reason this needed an architect rather than a worker: "re-read the surface once on the refusal path" cannot mean calling `getFrame()` again. That getter is SYNCHRONOUS over `frameRef.current`, written only by the 2000 ms poll, so a second call returns the SAME stale frame - a no-op fix that would pass a careless review and leave the defect. The re-read must be an ASYNC fetch, and `readSurfaceOnce` is the sanctioned one.
REJECTED - writing a fetch in live-goal-create.ts: `readSurfaceOnce` (policy-install-port.ts:35) already reads /affordances/read, and activation-port.ts:17-19 carries an explicit rail against a second fetch idiom for the same route.
REJECTED - adding a parameter to carry headers: `createGoalDispatcher` already takes `setup: LiveSetup`, whose `headers` field is documented at live-config.ts:38 as being for exactly this route.
REJECTED - landing the foreign scheduler tsc fix to unblock the e2e leg: it is a committed red in a package this row does not own; adopting it makes this row's red attribution unreadable. Disclose, run playwright directly, and leave it to its owner.
REJECTED - touching the e2e spec in any way: rail 2, and it is the spec that found both this defect and its predecessor.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 by architect-b63fabf3 at HEAD f3b94eaa on moe/work-2026-09-04.

1. THE PEER DIRT IS STILL LIVE. `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` shows ` M live-goal-create.ts`, ` M live-goal-create.test.ts`, ` M work-board.test.tsx`, ` M work-labels.ts`, ` M work-labels.test.ts`, and under ops/ ` M activation-port.ts`, ` M activation-port.test.ts`. BOTH files this row must edit are among them. That is the row's main operational hazard and it also breaks the usual restore-proof rule (see risks).

2. THE DEFECT, confirmed at the source. live-goal-create.ts:201-215: `createGoalDispatcher(setup: LiveSetup, getFrame: () => SurfaceFrame | null)`, comment "ONE read of the frame: the refusal must describe the same surface the offer was looked for on, not a later poll's", then `const frame = getFrame()`, `const offer = goalCreateOffer(frame, kind)`, and `if (offer === null) return { ok: false, report: goalCreateRefusal(frame, kind) }` - no dispatch, no second look.

3. WHY A SECOND `getFrame()` WOULD BE A NO-OP: live-goals.tsx:132 constructs it as `() => frameRef.current`; `frameRef.current` is written ONLY in the feed's `onFrame` callback (:89-92) driven by `POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2_000` (:33). Synchronous, poll-written. The re-read must be an async fetch.

4. THE HELPER EXISTS AND IS THE SANCTIONED ONE: `readSurfaceOnce(headers)` at policy-install-port.ts:35, "One read of the affordance surface, for the offer at the aggregate's current version", POSTing `/affordances/read` with `AbortSignal.timeout(SURFACE_TIMEOUT_MS)` and returning `frameOfSurface(await response.json())`. Re-exported at activation-port.ts:22, whose header states the rail: its `readSurfaceOnce` is IMPORTED rather than copied because "a second fetch idiom for the same route is exactly what this row's rail forbids".

5. THE HEADERS ARE ALREADY IN HAND: `LiveSetup.headers` (live-config.ts:38) is documented "Header values for the one route the transport does not carry (/affordances/read)" - the exact route. `createGoalDispatcher` already receives `setup`.

6. THE DAEMON IS NOT INVOLVED, confirming rail 1: `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["goal.create_with_source"] = ["project.activate"]` and the activate is COMMITTED when the refusal renders - the refusal never reaches the wire.

7. THE INJECTION CONVENTION for keeping the new arms deterministic: sessions-read.ts:86-87 (`readSessions`, `readClaims` optional with defaults) is this codebase's lazy-injection pattern. Passing the surface reader the same way lets the unit arms control it; importing `readSurfaceOnce` directly would leave them unable to.

8. THE FOREIGN RED: `pnpm test:e2e:browser` = `tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json && playwright test ...`, and the row records the tsc leg failing on `packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-reservation.ts(132,42): error TS18046: 'entry' is of type 'unknown'`. I read that file at plan time; the `value.meters.every((entry) => ...)` predicate is at that region. It is a committed red in another package.

9. FILE SIZES: live-goal-create.ts 229 (250 target - keep the change small), live-goals.tsx 174, activation-screen.tsx 216.
planningNotes.risks:
FIRST - THE RESTORE-PROOF RULE IS DIFFERENT ON THIS ROW AND THE USUAL ONE WOULD BE FALSE. Both owned files were ALREADY DIRTY with a peer's in-flight work before this row starts, so an empty `git diff` cannot be a drill's restore proof - it would be non-empty before, during and after, and cannot distinguish your mutation from theirs. Capture a SHA256 of each file BEFORE drilling and prove equality after, in a separate call. Do not quote an empty-diff proof here.

SECOND - THE NO-OP FIX THAT PASSES REVIEW. Calling `getFrame()` a second time looks exactly like "re-read the surface" and changes nothing, because the getter is synchronous over a 2 s-poll-written ref. Drill (i) is what catches it: remove the re-read and require the arm to go red with the stale-frame refusal string.

THIRD - A HALF FIX THAT STILL LIES. Re-reading for the offer LOOKUP but building the refusal from the STALE frame passes the obvious arm while telling the operator about a surface that no longer exists. Arm (2) and drill (ii) exist for exactly that, and DoD-4's invariant is what they pin.

FOURTH - PEER COLLISION. Another session holds edits in both files. Read their diff, edit around their hunks, never revert or regenerate from a HEAD copy, and if their work already touches `createGoalDispatcher`'s frame handling, coordinate by comment instead of racing. Their red is not yours: when a gate fails, check whether the failing arm names your change before attributing it.

FIFTH - DO NOT ADOPT THE SCHEDULER RED. It is committed, in another package, and blocks only the tsc leg of the browser e2e. Run playwright directly and disclose it; landing someone else's fix makes this row's attribution unreadable.

SIXTH - DO NOT TOUCH THE E2E SPEC (rail 2). No wait, no sleep, no relaxed assertion, no inflated timeout. `git diff --stat` it at the end and confirm zero changes - an operator hits this by clicking fast, and a spec that waits proves nothing.

SEVENTH - THE RE-READ CAN FAIL. `readSurfaceOnce` fetches with a timeout and can throw. A network failure on the refusal path must degrade to today's behaviour (refuse on the frame in hand), not surface a new error class to an operator who was simply told "create refused".

EIGHTH - A POLL AND A RE-READ CAN RACE, so the re-read could in principle answer an OLDER frame than the cached one. Decide whether the code prefers the newer and how it can tell; a version or timestamp comparison is honest, guessing is not.

NINTH - shared checkout. Peer dirt under .moe/ and .grok/ is NEVER a stop condition beyond the coordination above: note it, never revert, stash or `git add -A`. Report every path you touch in complete_step.modifiedFiles.
